title: Two Dining Philosophers
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Two Dining Philosophers scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: Places are circles and transitions are bars or rectangles, with arrows only between the two node kinds.
Initial tokens are visibly shown in the resource or state places needed to start the process.
The picture visibly supports the stated process progression through its marked places and transitions.
The net visibly expresses the scenario's buffer, shared resource, semaphore, cycle, or workflow choice control.
Tokens, labels, and arrows remain readable as a one-page Petri net.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the petri exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents the complete Two Dining Philosophers Petri net: Think1, Think2, Fork1, and Fork2 are initially marked; each philosopher has take/eat/release flow; and both take transitions require the two shared fork places. The stated Start1 → Finish1 firing sequence is visibly supported.

items.evidence: Places are circles, transitions are black bars, and all visible directed arcs connect a place to a transition or a transition to a place.
Visible tokens appear in Think1, Think2, Fork1, and Fork2, while Eat1 and Eat2 are unmarked.
Tokens in Think1, Fork1, and Fork2 visibly enable P1 takes forks; its output leads to Eat1, which then enables P1 releases forks and returns tokens to Think1 and both forks.
Fork1 and Fork2 are visibly shared by both philosophers' take and release transitions, expressing exclusive shared-resource control.
Tokens, place labels, transition labels, arrowheads, and the firing-sequence annotation are readable on one page despite some central arc overlap.
